107.1.2.head: خَيبَر
107.1.2.meaning: Khaybar, a fortified oasis north of Medina.

109.2.2.head: آيَة
109.2.2.meaning: His distinguishing sign. Here the word describes how the bearer of the standard can be recognised.

110.1.5.head: رَمَد
110.1.5.meaning: Soreness and inflammation of the eye.

111.1.2.head: هادى
111.1.2.meaning: To be led forward with someone supporting one's steps.

113.1.2.head: حُنَين
113.1.2.meaning: Hunayn, the valley of the encounter with Hawazin and Thaqif after the conquest of Mecca in 8 AH (630 CE).

113.1.5.head: كَثرَة
113.1.5.meaning: Their great numbers at Hunayn. Al-Sharafi sings kathratuhum, “their numbers”. The studio card has kathratuha, taking the force as a single body.

114.1.1.meaning: To waver or lose cohesion, here of ranks breaking under the assault.

115.1.4-5.head: ذَوو قَدَم
115.1.4-5.meaning: “People of prior standing”, those with a record of early service.

116.1.2.head: ثُلَّة
116.1.2.meaning: A group, here the few who held firm.

117.2.1.head: كال
117.2.1.meaning: To measure out by volume, transferred here from the market to battle.

118.1.1.head: عَرقَب
118.1.1.meaning: To disable a mount by wounding its hock.

119.2.4.head: ناضٍ
119.2.4.meaning: What flashes out uncovered, here understood as the cloud's lightning.

120.1.4.head: نَصر
120.1.4.meaning: Nasr, a branch of Hawazin named among the participants at Hunayn.

120.2.2.head: ثَقيف
120.2.2.meaning: Thaqif, the tribe of Ta'if involved in the Hunayn campaign.

121.1.5.head: كَرَب
121.1.5.meaning: To come close to doing something.

122.1.3.head: الصِّدّيق
122.1.3.meaning: Al-Siddiq, a title of Abu Bakr, the first caliph.

122.2.2.head: السَّقيفَة
122.2.2.meaning: The Saqifa, the portico of Banu Sa'ida in Medina where the succession was discussed.

123.1.2.head: فَلتَة
123.1.2.meaning: A sudden, unplanned event, echoing Umar's wording about the pledge.

123.2.3.head: الأَنصار
123.2.3.meaning: The Ansar or Helpers, the Medinans who received and supported Muhammad and the emigrants.

124.2.2.head: الزُّبَير
124.2.2.meaning: Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, an early Companion and a cousin of Muhammad.

124.2.4.head: الخُدرِيّ
124.2.4.meaning: Al-Khudri, Abu Sa'id, the Companion cited for the early pledge.

125.1.2.head: نَفِس
125.1.2.meaning: To begrudge another person what he has received.

125.2.2.head: اِفتات
125.2.2.meaning: To act unilaterally in a matter concerning others. The studio spells the form with a hamza.

127.2.6.head: ناعٍ
127.2.6.meaning: A bearer of news of someone's death.

128.1.1.head: أَعتَب
128.1.1.meaning: To be reconciled after a grievance.

128.1.5.head: اِنبَجَس
128.1.5.meaning: To burst forth, as water from a spring.

130.2.2.head: القِسطاس
130.2.2.meaning: An even balance, used here for judicial fairness.

131.1.3.head: الشَّيخان
131.1.3.meaning: The two elders, here Abu Bakr and Umar.

132.1.4.head: التَّفضيل
132.1.4.meaning: Giving Ali precedence over Abu Bakr and Umar in merit.

133.1.3-4.head: ذو النّورَين
133.1.3-4.meaning: Dhu al-Nurayn, “possessor of the two lights”, Uthman, who married two of Muhammad's daughters in succession.

134.2.1.head: السِّبط
134.2.1.meaning: A daughter's son, here Hasan as the Prophet's grandson.

135.2.3.head: شادَ
135.2.3.meaning: Were built or raised. The passive verb makes the ranks of honour into buildings.

136.2.6.head: داجٍ
136.2.6.meaning: The darkest part of the night.

140.1.5.head: سَبَق
140.1.5.meaning: A race to take the lead in good deeds.

141.1.1.head: أَخصَب
141.1.1.meaning: Those who bring plenty, pictured as fertile ground.

142.1.1-2.head: صِهر
142.1.1-2.meaning: Ahmad’s relatives by marriage. His wives included daughters of Abu Bakr and Umar. Uthman and Ali were his sons-in-law.

143.2.4.head: هانٍ
143.2.4.meaning: At ease or happy in living, with the final hamza softened in rhyme.

145.2.1.head: أَفناء
145.2.1.meaning: Open spaces and outskirts around a place.

147.1.1.head: أَعلاج
147.1.1.meaning: An abusive designation for rough outsiders in the poet's description.

147.1.6.head: لَجِب
147.1.6.meaning: Clamorous, noisy with a multitude of voices.

148.2.4.head: عَورات
148.2.4.meaning: Private matters or exposed vulnerabilities of a household.

151.2.3.head: ماد
151.2.3.meaning: To sway or shift beneath someone.

152.1.2.head: حُذَيفَة
152.1.2.meaning: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, the Companion associated with the report about Umar and the door holding back trials.

153.1.2-3.head: رَحى الشَّرّ
153.1.2-3.meaning: “The mill of evil”, a conflict that grinds down those caught in it.

153.1.5.head: واجِمَة
153.1.5.meaning: Stricken into silence by grief or fear.

154.1.4.head: شِرذِمَة
154.1.4.meaning: A handful of people, used contemptuously.

154.2.4.head: مَوالٍ
154.2.4.meaning: Clients or dependants, here set opposite their patrons.

155.2.3.head: سُدفَة
155.2.3.meaning: Darkness, one of two opposite senses recorded for the word.

158.1.3.head: أَوباش
158.1.3.meaning: A motley crowd, used here as an insult.

158.2.3.head: مِصر
158.2.3.meaning: Provincial garrison cities such as Basra and Kufa.

159.1.6.head: مُجتَهِد
159.1.6.meaning: Someone exercising considered judgement about what is right.

161.1.3-4.head: حَوارِيّ الرَّسول
161.1.3-4.meaning: “The Messenger's devoted helper”, a title given to al-Zubayr in hadith.

162.1.1-4.head: طَلحَة بن عُبَيد اللَّه
162.1.1-4.meaning: Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, a Companion wounded at Uhud and killed at the Camel in 36 AH (656 CE).

163.1.1.head: أُمُّنا
163.1.1.meaning: Aisha, daughter of Abu Bakr and one of Muhammad's wives, called Mothers of the Believers.

163.2.5.head: شانِئ
163.2.5.meaning: One who hates her. The regular word ends in a hamza.

164.1.5.head: خِدر
164.1.5.meaning: A screened compartment, here the camel litter in which Aisha rode.

166.2.1.head: رَأب
166.2.1.meaning: Mending a breach, physically or between people.

168.2.2.head: نُفوس
168.2.2.meaning: Lives, with an old association between the soul and the blood that flows from a wound.

168.2.4.head: شام
168.2.4.meaning: A verb for drawing or sheathing a sword. The outbreak of fighting favours drawing here.

169.2.1-2.head: أُمّ قَسطَل
169.2.1-2.meaning: “Mother of dust”, an old designation for calamity evoking the thick dust of battle.

170.1.3.meaning: Sheathe them. The call to hold back resolves the double meaning of the verb.

173.1.4-5.head: قَوس مُوَتَّرَة
173.1.4-5.meaning: A bow fitted with its bowstring and ready to shoot.

175.2.2.head: الخِطام
175.2.2.meaning: A camel's halter, here the one on Aisha's mount.

176.1.3.head: النَّقع
176.1.3.meaning: Dust raised by the movement of a battle.

176.1.5.head: أَجهَز
176.1.5.meaning: To finish off a wounded or fallen person.

177.1.6.head: سَلَب
177.1.6.meaning: Possessions taken from a defeated fighter.

178.2.3.head: اِطَّبى
178.2.3.meaning: To entice or draw someone to one's side.

178.2.4.head: نَزغ
178.2.4.meaning: An incitement or prompting to evil.

179.1.1.head: الشَّآم
179.1.1.meaning: Al-Sham, greater Syria, governed by Mu'awiya from Damascus.

180.1.2-3.head: ثارات عُثمان
180.1.2-3.meaning: “Vengeance for Uthman”, the demand for redress for the murdered caliph.

182.1.2-3.head: كاتِب الوَحي
182.1.2-3.meaning: “Scribe of revelation”, the title by which the poet introduces Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan.

183.1.1.head: العَبشَمِيّ
183.1.1.meaning: Abshami, belonging to Abd Shams, the ancestor of the Umayyad branch of Quraysh.

183.1.5.head: حَبوَة
183.1.5.meaning: A cloth used to bind the knees up to the body while sitting.

184.1.5.head: أَطَر
184.1.5.meaning: To bend or constrain something, here to bring a party back to allegiance.

185.1.4.head: صِفّين
185.1.4.meaning: Siffin, the site near the Euphrates of the battle in 37 AH (657 CE).

186.1.4-5.head: الشَّهر الحَرام
186.1.4-5.meaning: The sacred month, here Muharram in accounts of the Siffin truce.

189.1.5.head: قِرن
189.1.5.meaning: A matched opponent, one's equal in combat.

190.2.5.head: أَورى
190.2.5.meaning: To strike a spark and kindle a fire.

192.1.2.head: سِجال
192.1.2.meaning: A contest whose advantage alternates between the two sides.

193.2.4.head: مَآقٍ
193.2.4.meaning: The corners of the eyes where tears gather.

194.1.5.head: عَمّار
194.1.5.meaning: Ammar ibn Yasir, killed at Siffin on Ali's side and remembered in the report about a transgressing party.

194.2.5.head: باغٍ
194.2.5.meaning: A transgressor, echoing the wording of the report about Ammar.

195.2.4.head: أَجثى
195.2.4.meaning: To bring someone to their knees.

196.1.1-2.head: لاذَ
196.1.1-2.meaning: Took shelter on a rise in the ground. The verb conveys the search for protection.

197.2.1.head: مَصاحِف
197.2.1.meaning: Masahif, written copies of the Quran raised in the Siffin accounts.

198.2.2.head: المُهَيمِن
198.2.2.meaning: Al-Muhaymin, a divine name denoting oversight and protection.

199.1.3-4.meaning: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Abd Allah ibn Qays, the representative from the Iraqi side in the arbitration.

200.1.2.meaning: Amr ibn al-As, Mu'awiya's representative in the arbitration.

201.1.1-2.head: الحُكم لِلَّه
201.1.1-2.meaning: “Judgement belongs to God”, recalling the cry of those who rejected the arbitration.

202.1.4.head: الدّاران
202.1.4.meaning: “The two abodes”, this life and the life to come.

203.1.6.head: بَذَلَ
203.1.6.meaning: Was given up or sacrificed. The recited consonant is dh. The studio card has budilat with d, “was replaced”, so that severity takes the law’s place.

203.2.4.head: ناوى
203.2.4.meaning: To oppose or act as an adversary.

204.2.6.head: تَراقٍ
204.2.6.meaning: Collarbones, marking the boundary at the throat in the prophetic image.

205.2.1.meaning: To rival or lay claim to another's standing.

207.1.1.head: الرّاسِبِيّ
207.1.1.meaning: Al-Rasibi, Abd Allah ibn Wahb, chosen as leader by the seceders.

208.2.2.head: فَلس
208.2.2.meaning: A small copper coin, used as a measure of trifling value.

209.1.3.head: جُفاة
209.1.3.meaning: Harsh or uncultivated people, in the poet's judgement.

210.1.1-2.head: نَزَّلَ الآي
210.1.1-2.meaning: To apply the words or judgements of scripture to a particular group.

211.2.4.head: مارى
211.2.4.meaning: To dispute or argue a point with someone.

212.1.3-4.head: اِبن عَبّاس
212.1.3-4.meaning: Ibn Abbas, Abd Allah, cousin of both Muhammad and Ali, remembered for debating the seceders.

213.1.5.head: مُناجَزَة
213.1.5.meaning: An immediate clash or armed encounter.

214.1.3.head: فَيء
214.1.3.meaning: Fay', public revenue from which a community or its members might receive a share.

215.1.2.head: سَدَر
215.1.2.meaning: To persist heedlessly, without seeing the consequences.

215.2.5.head: قانٍ
215.2.5.meaning: Deep crimson, the colour of shed blood.

216.2.4.head: المَعصوم
216.2.4.meaning: One whom God preserves from error. Here the title belongs to Muhammad as bearer of revelation.

218.1.5-6.head: وَهَن
218.1.5-6.meaning: Do not falter or lose strength.

219.1.1.head: وَحَّش
219.1.1.meaning: To fling away what one is holding, especially one's arms.

219.1.2-3.head: القَنا الخَطِّيّ
219.1.2-3.meaning: Khatt spears, named for the east Arabian coastal district associated with the spear trade.

220.1.1.head: شَجَر
220.1.1.meaning: To pierce or impale with a spear.

221.1.1-2.head: أَخو مُراد
221.1.1-2.meaning: “Brother of Murad”, a man of the Murad tribe, here Ali's assassin Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam.

221.1.3.head: لَحا
221.1.3.meaning: A curse calling disgrace upon the person addressed.

221.1.6.head: غُدَر
221.1.6.meaning: A treacherous person, an emphatic term of reproach.

222.1.1.head: خَضَّب
222.1.1.meaning: To dye, ordinarily the hair, here with blood.

223.2.5.head: قَفّى
223.2.5.meaning: To turn one's back to it in this image.

224.1.4-5.head: شَهر الصِّيام
224.1.4-5.meaning: Ramadan, the fasting month in which Ali was attacked at Kufa in 40 AH (661 CE).

225.1.1-2.head: يا ضَربَة
225.1.1-2.meaning: “What a blow”, the opening of a pointed rejoinder to verse attributed to Imran ibn Hittan.

226.2.3.head: هَفا
226.2.3.meaning: To yearn towards or fly in longing.

227.1.1-2.head: فاضَتِ النَّفس
227.1.1-2.meaning: “The soul flowed out”, a gentle way of saying that someone died.

228.1.4.head: بِضع
228.1.4.meaning: A few, conventionally a number from three to nine.

231.1.3-4.head: السُّنَّة البَيضاء
231.1.3-4.meaning: “The radiant Sunna”, Muhammad's practice pictured as a visible source of guidance.

232.2.4.head: أَصمى
232.2.4.meaning: To strike a fatal blow, used figuratively of refuting a practice.

233.2.5.head: تَأَسٍّ
233.2.5.meaning: Following an example in one's own actions.

234.1.3.head: عِمران
234.1.3.meaning: Imran ibn Husayn, the Companion whose comment on Ali's prayer is reported by Mutarrif.

235.2.2-3.head: مُتعَة الحَجّ
235.2.2-3.meaning: Mut'at al-hajj, combining the lesser and greater pilgrimages in one journey. Ali's reported invocation names both rites.

236.2.4.head: أَوالٍ
236.2.4.meaning: The first members of a community, its forebears.

238.1.4.head: غالٍ
238.1.4.meaning: Those judged to have exceeded the bounds of veneration, here by ascribing divinity.

239.1.5.head: عِصمَة
239.1.5.meaning: Isma, divine protection against sin or error, understood differently in different traditions.

240.2.2.head: فُهوم
240.2.2.meaning: Particular insights or ways of understanding scripture.

241.1.4.head: الأُلى
241.1.4.meaning: An older relative pronoun meaning “those who”.

242.1.1.head: صَحيفَة
242.1.1.meaning: Sahifa, a written sheet. The preceding verse places it in Ali’s sword scabbard.

243.1.3-4.head: أَبو الهَيّاج
243.1.3-4.meaning: Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi, Hayyan ibn Husayn, who transmits the commission from Ali in Muslim.

244.2.4.head: شاد
244.2.4.meaning: To build up or raise conspicuously.

245.2.4.head: الإِسناد
245.2.4.meaning: Isnad, the chain of transmitters by which a report is traced to its source.

246.2.2.head: الحَنَفِيّ
246.2.2.meaning: Al-Hanafi, Muhammad ibn Ali, called Ibn al-Hanafiyya after his mother's Banu Hanifa affiliation.

246.2.4.head: عازٍ
246.2.4.meaning: One who attributes a report to its transmitter.

247.2.5.head: مُقرِئ
247.2.5.meaning: Muqri', a teacher of Quranic recitation. The rhyme softens the final hamza.

248.1.5-6.head: أَبو حَسَن
248.1.5-6.meaning: Abu Hasan, Ali's name as the father of Hasan.

248.2.3.head: عَدن
248.2.3.meaning: Eden or abiding residence, in a Quranic expression for the gardens of Paradise.

250.2.4.head: النَّدب
250.2.4.meaning: The noble man quick to respond, here Ali.

251.1.2.head: النَّصب
251.1.2.meaning: Nasb, a term in historical religious controversy for hostility to Ali or his family.

252.2.1.head: جَحَد
252.2.1.meaning: To deny what the speaker regards as plainly established.
